title: Enterprise Prospect Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Priya Singh
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a single-source reference for AEs, solution engineers, and customer-facing GTM teams working enterprise prospects. It bundles positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guidance, two short case studies with outcomes, and a prospect-focused Security FAQ. Use this to accelerate discovery, handle common objections, and shorten time-to-close for Dedicated and Private deals.

Audience:
- Account Executives (AEs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Sales Engineers and Customer Success Engs supporting POCs
- Revenue operations and enablement

One-line positioning:
Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while giving engineering teams full control over performance, cost, and compliance.

Core value pillars (talking points):
- Predictable performance and SLAs: Dedicated pools, SLO-driven routing, and operational fallbacks reduce production risk.
- Cost controls and optimization: Batching, caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token costs without large accuracy regressions.
- Deployment flexibility: Hosted, Reserved (Dedicated), and Private (VPC/on-prem) models with consistent API and rollout tooling.
- Developer experience: Fast SDKs, streaming, function/tool-calling, and strong observability for debugging and cost attribution.
- Security & compliance: KMS integrations, audit logs, and regional deployments for data residency.

Target personas and value props (short):
- ML Platform / Infra leaders: predictable TCO, capacity commitments, private deployment options, and observability hooks for governance.
- Product & Engineering: low-latency inference, simple SDKs, and minimal infra work to integrate.
- Security / Compliance: private deployment patterns, KMS/HSM support, and standardized evidence for audits.

Competitive brief (summary and quick rebuts):
Top competitors: Generic cloud-managed model endpoints, LLM API providers, and self-hosted inference runtimes.
Key differentiators vs. competitors:
- Versus Managed Cloud Endpoints: Redwood offers opinionated runtime optimizations (continuous batching/KV caching, kernel-selection) plus a single interface across hosting and private deployments.
- Versus LLM API providers: We surface unit economics tooling (batching/caching suggestions, quantization profiles) and Dedicated capacity with SLAs for enterprise workloads.
- Versus Self-hosted Runtimes: We provide the orchestration, rollout tooling, and multi-region failover without requiring customers to run the full control plane.

Competitive comparison (table):
Service | Strength | Typical loss angle | Rebuttal
Redwood Inference | Dedicated + Private options, cost tooling, developer UX | Newer company; integration lift for Private | Emphasize production telemetry, reference customers, and migration guides + professional services.
Cloud Endpoint (CLOUD-A) | Broad infra ecosystem | Cost per token, opaque performance for LLMs | Call out model-and-runtime optimizations and unit-cost reductions.
LLM API (API-X) | Simple API, large models | No dedicated capacity or private deployment | Emphasize SLAs, private deployments, and security controls.
Open-source runtime | Cost flexible and customizable | Operates as infra burden, slower time-to-production | Redwood reduces ops burden with a managed control plane and expert migration support.

Pitch deck: structure and slide notes (recommended):
1) Title & TL;DR (1 slide): one-sentence value prop + top 3 benefits (latency, cost, compliance).
2) Customer problem (1 slide): real-world examples and metrics (slow tail latency, unpredictible costs, audit requirements).
3) Redwood solution (2 slides): architecture diagram for Hosted/Dedicated/Private + short bullets for runtime features (batching, caching, kernel selection).
4) Technical differentiators (1 slide): benchmarks (p50/p95 latency), quantization and cost savings examples.
5) Pricing models & expected TCO (1 slide): example scenarios for self-serve vs Dedicated commitment.
6) Security & compliance (1 slide): highlights (KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO, data residency).
7) Case studies (1-2 slides): short outcomes with KPIs.
8) Deployment and onboarding plan (1 slide): PoC steps, timelines, owners.
9) Pricing ask / next steps (1 slide): clear CTA and procurement contacts.

Pitch deck best practices and checklist:
- Keep slides with clear, verifiable metrics.
- Include an architecture diagram tailored to the prospect (VPC, on-prem details).
- Bring a technical fallback plan: pre-approved model variants or burst capacity options.
- Pre-load prospective prompts for a live demo to show latency and cost.

Pricing guidance (models and examples):
Pricing models we use:
- Hosted (usage-based): per-token generation + per-embedding units + optional observability add-ons.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual reserved GPU capacity with overage rates and burst tiers.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support tiers + professional services + optional on-prem packaging.

Example pricing scenarios (table):
Scenario | Typical customer | Pricing model | Expected cost drivers
Small PLG app | Seed-stage startup | Hosted usage | token volume, avg response length, embedding requests
Growth SaaS | Mid-market product | Dedicated (monthly commit) | committed throughput, storage for KV cache, SLA tier
Regulated enterprise | Financial / Healthcare | Private + support | deployment packaging, audit evidence, integration time

Negotiation guidance and discount levers:
- Commit to multi-month/annual Dedicated capacity for tiered discounts.
- Bundled professional services and onboarding credits for Private customers.
- Observatory retention and advanced support as add-on to protect margin.
- Provide a trial credit for Hosted API plus a 30-day Dedicated pilot at discounted rate to prove value.

Case studies (short):
1) FinTech Corp (Dedicated deployment)
- Customer problem: inconsistent response latency during peak trading windows; strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Redwood deployment: Dedicated GPU pool in customer VPC, KMS-managed keys, and per-route SLOs.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 1.2s to 300ms, per-token cost down 28% through batching and cache warm-ups, compliance audit passed with required evidence in 6 weeks.

2) B2B SaaS (Hosted -> Dedicated upgrade)
- Customer problem: early product used Hosted API; growth caused unpredictable costs and occasional tail latency spikes.
- Redwood deployment: initial Hosted integration, then 3-month transition to Dedicated reserved capacity with telemetry-driven quantization profile.
- Outcome: monthly inference cost reduced 42% after Dedicated commit, SLA-backed uptime improved reliability during peak launches.

Security FAQ (prospect-facing, short answers):
Q: Where is customer data stored and how can we meet data residency requirements?
A: Redwood supports region-specific deployments and VPC Private deployment options. For Private installs we can package on-prem or run in customer cloud region and provide evidence of controls.

Q: How do you protect customer keys and secrets?
A: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support HSM-based key wraps for Private deployments. Keys are never stored in plaintext in the control plane.

Q: Can you provide audit evidence for SOC/ISO assessments?
A: Yes. We maintain SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 artifacts for relevant systems. For Private customers we provide tailored evidence and support audit workflows.

Q: How do you handle model hallucination and quality regressions?
A: We provide eval harnesses, per-model quality regression alerts, and the ability to pin model versions and fallback policies. Solutions teams can add prompt guards and reranking layers.

Q: What SLAs do you offer?
A: Hosted API offers standard availability SLAs; Dedicated customers receive SLA commitments by contract (uptime and latency SLOs). Specific SLA terms live in the contract and can be tiered by commitment.

Q: How do you minimize cost while preserving quality?
A: We recommend batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization profiles tailored to the workload - we provide tooling and prescriptive configs that our Optimize team validates.

Q: How are customer logs and audit trails retained?
A: Audit logs are collected and can be configured for retention length per customer policy. For Private deployments logs are stored in the customer-managed logging destination when required.

POC / Demo plan (recommended 6-8 week structure):
1) Week 0: Discovery (stakeholders, security checklist, success metrics).
2) Week 1-2: Proof-of-Concept setup (choose Hosted pilot or Dedicated pilot, seed prompts, instrumentation).
3) Week 3-4: Tuning (batching, cache warming, quantization experiments, integration).
4) Week 5-6: Validation (load test, SLO checks, security evidence pack).
5) Week 7-8: Decision and procurement (pricing proposal, procurement support, onboarding plan).

Objection handling (common):
- "We can self-host": Acknowledge control benefits, then show total cost of ownership and time-to-production advantages with Redwood, and offer a migration plan + POC.
- "We need strict compliance": Offer Private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit evidence timeline.
- "Token costs are too high": Walk through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations and provide example TCO scenarios from comparable customers.
